content:
Sahana Iyer: perf-canary integration question for profile pack work — what do we want to *block merges* on vs just *warn*? Need to lock this before we wire up PR checks. Context: perf-canary PR https://github.com/perf-canary/pr-388 and Linear tasks ENG-4930 (gating) + ENG-4931 (tags/metrics).

Marcus Reed: +1. I’m worried we’ll block everything on noise unless we’re strict about when we run and what metric we gate on.

Rina Kobayashi: from benchmark-lab side we can give you stable-ish runs for H100/L40S if we keep matrix small. But concurrency + mixed workload is still spiky.

Allison Grant: reminder: we’re also adding profile_id/profile_version tags to histograms (PR https://github.com/redwood/pr-24935). If canary is comparing latency deltas, it needs to be profile-aware or it’ll be useless.

Noah Patel: IMO: correctness/config validity should be hard block (schema validation, profile selection determinism, no missing defaults). Perf deltas should block only if the signal is strong and aligned w/ SLO guardrails.

Sahana Iyer: specific proposal (draft):
1) Always block: profile schema invalid, selection nondeterministic, profile_version pin breaks startup, missing required tags for canary compare.
2) Perf: block if p99 latency regression > X% AND absolute p99 over SLO gate for canary cohort.
3) Otherwise warn (Slack + PR comment) w/ links to dashboards.
Thoughts on thresholds and what “strong signal” means?

Sofia Ivanova: for scheduler changes, p99 is the one that bites us. But I don’t want to block on p99 deltas on tiny sample sizes. Can we gate on p95 for merge-block and p99 as warn + required follow-up?

Marcus Reed: historically p95 is stable-ish; p99 is the noise monster. But… the incident risk is p99. So maybe: p95 hard gate, p99 soft gate but paging threshold for canary.

Rafael Mendes: from SRE angle: merge gating should catch “obvious regression” only. Rollout gating (Hosted canary) should be stricter and include p99 + error rate + queueing time.

Allison Grant: + queueing. A lot of “p99 got worse” is really scheduler_queue_ms exploding, not compute. If perf-canary can capture queue_ms distribution, that helps triage.

Omar El-Sayed: queue_ms + kv_cache metrics are getting tagged; but for canary we can do at least: scheduler_queue_ms p95/p99 and request_latency_ms p95/p99. Also kernel_fallback_rate. If fallbacks spike, latency deltas are expected.

Rina Kobayashi: we can provide canary artifacts keyed by (sku, model, workload_bucket, profile_version, git_sha). But we should constrain workloads for merge gating. Suggest 2 buckets per SKU:
- “short” (prefill small, decode small)
- “mixed” (prefill variable, decode medium)
Not doing the “long context” bucket in merge gate.

Sahana Iyer: ok. So for merge gate matrix: H100 + L40S, 2 buckets each, 1 model family each (ex: llama-ish 8B-ish for L40S, 70B-ish for H100)?

Marcus Reed: works. Also run each config twice and take median? That helps a lot.

Rina Kobayashi: yes, but runtime doubles. Merge gate needs to finish < 30m or people will revolt.

Connor O'Brien: :wave: adding release engineering perspective — if it blocks merges, it must be deterministic-ish. If it’s flaky, we’ll end up with everyone bypassing checks. Prefer fewer hard blocks.

Noah Patel: to make it deterministic: hard gate only on *relative delta + minimum effect size*. Example:
- If p95 regression > 8% AND absolute delta > 15ms, block.
- If error rate increases > 0.2% absolute, block.
Then p99 we track but don’t block merges.

Sofia Ivanova: can we also block if scheduler_queue_ms p95 doubles? That’s almost always a real issue.

Allison Grant: yes, but pick a floor. Like only if queue_ms p95 > 25ms and >2x baseline. Otherwise we’ll block on low baseline jitter (e.g., 1ms -> 3ms).

Omar El-Sayed: kernel fallback should be hard gate? If fallback rate goes from ~0 to 20% we basically changed the runtime behavior.

Marcus Reed: I’d make kernel_fallback_rate a warn-only unless it’s correlated with latency regression. Sometimes it’s “expected” when we tweak conditions (and it doesn’t always hurt).

Rafael Mendes: suggest:
- WARN on fallback rate > 5% or delta > 3% absolute.
- BLOCK only if fallback rate > 15% *and* p95 regresses beyond threshold.

Sahana Iyer: that seems reasonable.

perf-canary bot: Buildkite pipeline `perf-canary/pr` (PR #388) updated: adds support for `--compare=baseline` and posts summary to Slack channel #eng-runtime.

Sahana Iyer: thanks bot :)

Sahana Iyer: more questions:
- Should B200 be allowed-to-fail for now? (we have smoke suite PR https://github.com/benchmark-lab/pr-927 flagged allowed-to-fail)
- Should perf-canary block merges for *profile pack config changes* but not for general runtime code changes?

Connor O'Brien: B200 should definitely be allowed-to-fail until Infra locks baseline driver/CUDA. We can’t block mainline on “bring-up noise”.

Noah Patel: +1. For B200, hard gate is “compatibility gate triggers correctly” (i.e. refuse unsafe defaults unless explicitly pinned). Perf should be informational.

Rina Kobayashi: agree. B200 suite should run nightly + on-demand, not on every PR.

Marcus Reed: re: block only for config changes — I’d avoid special casing by path, but we can change severity based on label. Eg if PR has `profile-pack` label then require perf-canary green. Otherwise just post metrics.

Sahana Iyer: label-based gating is doable.

Allison Grant: + we should require profile_id/profile_version tags present on emitted metrics as a “blocker” for any PR that touches observability / histograms. Otherwise we keep shipping untagged metrics and canary compare breaks.

Omar El-Sayed: I can add a unit/integration test that asserts `profile_id` tag exists on request_latency_ms histogram in runtime env. That could be part of the “block always” bucket.

Sofia Ivanova: + queueing vs compute separation in traces is landing soon (Julian’s PR). But for canary, histograms are enough.

Rafael Mendes: also want explicit behavior: when canary fails (merge gate) it should include: baseline version, candidate version, delta, and link to result artifact. Not just “red.”

Sahana Iyer: yep, we’ll have the PR check comment include:
- sku
- workload_bucket
- baseline profile_version + git sha
- candidate profile_version + git sha
- p50/p95/p99 latency deltas
- scheduler_queue_ms deltas
- kernel_fallback_rate
- result artifact link (S3)

Marcus Reed: what about throughput? tokens/sec regression is also a problem.

Noah Patel: I’d include throughput but not gate on it initially. Throughput sometimes improves at expense of latency (or vice versa). We should align gating w/ SLOs (latency + error). Throughput is for capacity planning.

Allison Grant: +1. Add tokens/sec as FYI.

Sahana Iyer: ok, summarizing (unless objections):
MERGE BLOCKERS (when perf-canary runs):
- Schema/validation: invalid profile config; selection nondeterminism; missing required fields; startup fails with profile_version pin.
- Observability contract: request_latency_ms histogram MUST include tags `profile_id`, `profile_version`, `sku` (for PRs w/ `profile-pack` label).
- Perf regression: p95 latency regression > 8% AND absolute delta > 15ms for any gated bucket on H100/L40S.
- Queueing: scheduler_queue_ms p95 > 25ms AND >2x baseline.
- Errors: error rate +0.2% absolute (timeouts/OOMs/etc), any bucket.
SOFT WARNINGS:
- p99 regression > 10% (post warning + ask for follow-up)
- kernel_fallback_rate delta > 3% or absolute > 5%
- tokens/sec regression > 8%
B200:
- Allowed-to-fail (runs nightly or on-demand), except compatibility gate correctness.
If ok, I’ll update ENG-4930 description + comment on perf-canary PR.

Connor O'Brien: looks good. Please also add “how to rerun canary” to the PR template or check output.

Rina Kobayashi: works for benchmark-lab. For the merge gate, please keep it to <= 4 total runs (H100 short/mixed, L40S short/mixed) and fixed seed.

Marcus Reed: +1. Also have the check print “noise budget” (like standard deviation) eventually, but not a blocker.

Allison Grant: fine by me. Tag requirements as blockers will force people to keep things consistent.

Rafael Mendes: thumbs up. This is aligned with rollout SLO guardrails; merge gate is “catch big issues,” rollout is “protect prod.”

Sahana Iyer: cool. I’ll push updates and ping when the check is live.

perf-canary bot: Reminder: `perf-canary/pr` can be rerun with `/bk rerun perf-canary/pr` (requires `eng-runtime` group).
